title: Measure and remove redundant symbol-name tokens from signatures

state.decision_rationale: Accepted by omitting signatures identical to symbol names while retaining nonredundant signatures.

feedback.verbatim: Omit Redundant Signatures: In the symbol outlines, you occasionally repeat the name in the signature (e.g., name="name" ... signature="name: string"). For massive codebases, stripping the name from the signature if it matches the name field could shave off a few thousand tokens.
feedback.normalized_claim: Avoid repeating a symbol's name inside its signature when the name is already encoded as a separate field and the signature remains unambiguous without it.

current_behavior: Symbol records emit name and analyzer-provided signature as separate attributes.
The renderer preserves the signature returned by the outline analyzer rather than attempting language-specific normalization.
The sample function record repeats double in name=double and signature=double(value: number): number.

proposal.summary: Measure signature-name duplication and evaluate a reversible, language-aware normalization that removes only provably redundant name tokens.
candidate_changes: Collect corpus statistics for signature repetition and tokenizer-specific savings before changing the grammar.
Define structured signature fields such as parameters, return type, modifiers, and type annotation instead of rewriting analyzer strings heuristically.
Allow a compact signature_tail field whose documented interpretation prepends the separate symbol name.
Retain full signatures when constructors, operators, overloads, generics, computed names, destructuring, or language syntax make removal ambiguous.
non_goals: Do not strip substrings with a language-agnostic text replacement.
Do not reduce human readability or reconstruction accuracy for negligible measured savings.
Do not change the current symbol grammar during feedback intake.

questions: How often do analyzer signatures repeat the exact name across supported languages?
How many model tokens would normalization save on small, medium, and large packets?
Can the original display signature be reconstructed without language-specific guessing?
Would structured signature fields help reasoning more than a compact opaque tail?
risks: Naive stripping may corrupt constructors, operators, overloads, generic signatures, or fields whose names are syntactically meaningful.
A more complex signature grammar may cost more tokens than it saves.
Diverging from analyzer-native signatures can make debugging and cross-checking harder.
evidence_needed: A multi-language corpus of actual Graft outline signatures.
Exact tokenizer counts before and after each normalization design.
Round-trip or semantic-equivalence tests for functions, methods, fields, constructors, operators, and overloads.
Blind model comparison for symbol-understanding accuracy.
